Overview

Director, Digital & Information Management is a leadership role responsible for developing and implementing the digital strategy and information management framework for one of our major new build projects. The role is responsible for developing and implementing the digital strategy and information management framework for this project. The Director reports functionally to the Vice-President, Digital Solutions and operationally to the Project Director.

This Director ensures that all project data, documentation, and digital systems are integrated, secure, and aligned with company standards, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and project objectives. The position drives digital transformation to enable efficient collaboration, lifecycle data management, and regulatory compliance across engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning phases.

Key responsibilities include leading project teams, developing work execution plans, recruiting and assigning team members, managing project deliverables, organizational structure, budget, schedule, risk management, and overseeing people forecasting and levelling for the project.

Your role

Proven ability to lead teams, manage direct reports, and support project delivery organizations through complex digital initiatives.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Technology Risk Assessments
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 278455

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Scotiabank is seeking a transformational senior leader to modernize how technology and cybersecurity risks are assessed across the Bank. Reporting to the Vice President, IT Governance & Risk Oversight within the Office of the Chief Information Officer, the Senior Director, Technology Risk Assessments leads Scotiabank's global first-line technology and cybersecurity assessment capability relating to the Bank’s Threat Risk Assessments and Vendor Security Review processes.

The Senior Director brings the Bank's Threat Risk Assessment and Vendor Security Review processes under one leadership responsibility, creating an integrated approach to assessing internally developed technology solutions and third-party technology services. Together, these form an integrated Assessment Authority: one first-line capability for technology and cybersecurity assessment that preserves specialized expertise while introducing common leadership and strategic direction, coordinated intake and triage, consistent assessment methods and risk language, shared evidence and quality principles, reusable platform and security patterns, stronger risk reporting and traceability, modern workflows and structured data, and progressive use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automation.

This role is broader than traditional assessment delivery. It is an enterprise leadership and transformation opportunity to turn fragmented, document-heavy processes into an integrated, risk-based and evidence-informed assessment lifecycle. It brings together technology risk, cybersecurity, security advisory, third-party risk, cloud and AI security, Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) modernization, adoption of ServiceNow Integrated Risk Management (IRM), data and automation, and leadership of a global team.

You Will Shape And Lead Six Connected Themes

Integrated Assessment Authority: One accountable leadership model for Threat Risk Assessment (TRA) and Vendor Security Review (VSR), with common direction, methods and risk language across specialized assessment teams.
Shift-left security assessment: Technology and cybersecurity risks identified and addressed earlier in architecture, design and delivery, when they are least costly to resolve.
Platform and application assessment: A two-level model that assesses shared platforms once and focuses application and vendor assessments on what is genuinely specific.
Evidence-informed risk decisions: Risk conclusions grounded in structured, verifiable evidence and consistent rating criteria rather than document volume.
Modern workflow, data and automation: Assessments run through modern ServiceNow IRM workflows, supported by structured data and the progressive use of AI and automation.
Portfolio risk insight: Clear, traceable reporting that surfaces recurring and systemic risks across the Bank's technology and third-party portfolio.

The Platform And Application Model Works At Two Levels

Horizontal assessments evaluate common platforms, shared services and approved technology patterns once, so related controls and evidence can be reused.
Vertical assessments evaluate the application, workload, project, vendor or material change, and focus on specific deviations, exposures and residual risks

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

Lead the existing TRA and VSR capabilities under one senior leadership model, preserving specialized expertise while establishing common direction, coordinated intake and triage, and shared standards.
Define and maintain consistent assessment methodology, risk-rating criteria, quality requirements, evidence principles and finding taxonomies, aligned to the Bank's technology control objectives and enterprise control library and to recognized frameworks such as the National Institute of Standards and Technology Cybersecurity Framework (NIST CSF), ISO/IEC 27001 and the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS).
Embed technology and cybersecurity assessment earlier in architecture, design and technology delivery, including the Bank's delivery framework, architecture review processes and Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
Establish reusable security and platform patterns that allow downstream assessments to inherit approved baselines.
Assess material application-specific and vendor-specific risks, including data, identity, integration, architecture, exposure and residual risk.
Strengthen threat modelling and scenario-based risk analysis, using recognized approaches such as STRIDE and MITRE ATT&CK.
Act as the business owner for the technology-risk assessment capability within ServiceNow IRM, defining assessment requirements, workflows and data needs while working with the technical platform team, which owns platform configuration and delivery.
Lead the assessment-domain transition from legacy processes and repositories into modern IRM workflows, preserving application-to-assessment and application-to-risk traceability and establishing clear data-quality requirements.
Define risk-based triggers for reassessment following material change, significant vulnerability, control failure or deviation from an approved pattern.
Establish targeted post-implementation assurance for selected material controls, using authoritative evidence from accountable control owners and specialist functions.
Prioritize appropriate AI and automation opportunities across intake, triage, context extraction, pattern matching, assessment drafting, evidence orchestration and portfolio insight, in alignment with the Bank's enterprise artificial intelligence and technology-risk automation initiatives.
Identify recurring and systemic risks across the assessment portfolio and provide clear risk insight to technology leaders and governance forums.
Produce assessment outcomes that are timely, consistent, traceable, evidence-informed and defensible for regulatory, second-line, quality assurance and Internal Audit review, including under the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) Guideline B-13 and the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) Part 500 cybersecurity regulation, where applicable.
Lead and develop a large, multidisciplinary and geographically distributed team, building capabilities in security advisory, cloud and AI security, third-party security risk, methodology, data and automation..

Critical Partnerships

Success depends on strong partnerships across the Bank's three lines of defense. Each partner keeps its established mandate, and the Senior Director works with them to ensure that assessment conclusions are well-informed and aligned. Key partners include:

Technology leadership: Chief Information Officers (CIOs) and their delivery, architecture and engineering teams, the primary clients of the assessment capability.
Cybersecurity and architecture: The Office of the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and Enterprise Architecture, to align security standards, patterns and design guidance.
Control owners and control testing: Teams that implement and operate controls, and the Bank's technology control testing function, whose evidence informs assessment conclusions.
Technology risk management: Technology risk teams and Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) teams, which manage and aggregate technology risk across the Bank.
Platform and automation: The ServiceNow IRM platform and implementation teams, and the Bank's enterprise artificial intelligence and technology-risk automation initiatives, to ensure aligned workflows and data.
Governance and reporting: IT risk governance, issue management and reporting teams within the Office of the Chief Information Officer.
Independent oversight: Second-line risk management, Internal Quality Assurance (IQA) and Internal Audit, which provide independent challenge and assurance, and the teams that manage the Bank's regulatory relationships

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security or a related field.
10+ years of progressive experience in technology risk, cybersecurity or risk assessment, including senior leadership of technology or cybersecurity risk assessment functions.
Deep expertise in security advisory, assessment methodology and threat modelling at enterprise scale.
Strong experience in third-party and vendor security risk, and in cloud, AI, application and platform security.
A track record of leading enterprise GRC transformation, including with ServiceNow IRM or a comparable GRC platform, from business requirements through adoption.
Strong understanding of development, security and operations (DevSecOps) practices and secure-by-design principles.
Experience engaging regulators and Internal Audit in a highly regulated environment, ideally financial services.
Proven ability to lead large, distributed teams and to lead through influence across federated organizations and with senior technology executives.

Preferred Experience

Advanced degree or professional certifications such as Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC) or Certified Information Security Manager (CISM).
Experience leading platform- and pattern-based assessment models that allow controls to be inherited across applications and workloads.
Hands-on experience with risk data, evidence orchestration and workflow automation, including integrations with security tooling.
Familiarity with AI, machine learning and agentic AI applications in GRC, such as intake triage, artifact analysis, control mapping and risk-theme identification.
Experience applying structured risk-rating criteria, calibration and quantitative risk techniques.
Experience partnering with control-testing functions to integrate authoritative control evidence into risk assessment, ideally within a large financial institution

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.
Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days and benefits will start on day one.
Community Engagement - no matter where you choose to work from; we offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs such as hackathons, contests, Humans of Digital and much more.

Finance and controls. Own month-end close, financial reporting, external audit and internal controls across our Canada and US entities.
Payments finance operations. You don't reconcile every transaction yourself, but you own the whole mechanism and the outcome of every exception:
End-to-end reconciliation across internal transaction records, the user balance ledger, payment processor records and bank statements
Settlement and payouts: correct amounts, timing, receiving entities and approval authority
Exceptions such as missing orders, duplicate payments, delayed settlements, fee differences and refunds not received, traced and closed out
Clear accounting and control boundaries between company operating funds, user funds and settlement funds
Treasury and liquidity: funds kept safe, liquidity sufficient and settlements accurate, with strong bank and payment-processor relationships

Digital transformation. Find the manual, error-prone steps in finance and payment operations, then work with product and engineering to automate them and to monitor for fund discrepancies, late settlements and unusual transactions.
Team. Lead, coach and grow the finance team, starting with the Financial Controller.
Fundraising and investments. Partner with the CEO on fundraising, board and investor materials and the numbers behind major decisions; oversee corporate investments.
Compliance, over time. Work with our compliance lead on fund controls, audit evidence and bank requirements, with room to take on more compliance responsibility as you grow into the role.

This is a startup seat: you manage the team and do the work yourself.

While the team is still being built, you dig into the books, chase discrepancies and deal with banks and payment processors yourself

CPA designation, with a strong accounting and Controller foundation
Experience leading a full finance function and managing a team

Experience in payments, fintech or other regulated businesses, working with compliance on fund controls, audit evidence and bank requirements
SQL, BI or API data experience (real implementations matter more than tool names)
Multi-entity finance across Canada and the US
Fundraising, bank credit facilities, data rooms, or investor and board communication
Business analytics: runway, unit economics and operating KPIs

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance & CFO, Canadian Personal & Small Business Banking (CPSB), the Associate Vice President leads Finance support for Real Estate Secured Lending (RESL), Specialized Sales Force (SSF), Operations and the Chief Operating Officer (COO) organization. The role is the senior Finance partner to the SVP, RESL; SVP, Specialized Sales Force; and SVP & COO, CPSB, connecting strategy with financial outcomes across significant revenue, balance sheet, expense and investment portfolios.

The role provides forward-looking advice and independent challenge on growth, profitability, productivity, transformation and resource allocation. It brings an enterprise perspective to decisions, identifies opportunities for value creation and maintains strong financial management, controls and performance discipline.

As a member of TD's leadership team, the AVP sets high ethical and performance standards, develops talent and collaborates across the Bank to deliver sustainable results. The role requires strategic insight, business acumen, sound judgment and integrity.

Position-specific Accountabilities

Lead portfolio planning, forecasting, reporting and performance management. Develop driver-based forecasts and scenarios, explain variances, and translate risks and opportunities into executive insight and recommended actions.
Advise and independently challenge RESL pricing and offers. Assess volume, retention, margin and risk-adjusted return trade-offs, considering funding costs, customer behaviour and competition.
Lead SSF financial planning and analysis, including MMS and broker channel financials and compensation models. Evaluate acquisition costs, incentives, conversion, retention and lifetime profitability; advise on compensation changes and channel mix across branch, specialist, broker and digital distribution.
Assess portfolio economics across volumes, market share, margins, credit, funding, expenses and returns. Analyze profitability by product, segment and origination cohort, isolating mix, pricing, renewals and runoff. Partner with Treasury, Risk, Product and Distribution on rate scenarios, funding and capital implications.
Advise on investment prioritization and allocation of capital, expense and capacity. Challenge business cases, returns, costs and milestones; track benefits and cross-CPSB dependencies and trade-offs. Recommend reprioritization when economics or delivery assumptions change.
Analyze operational cost drivers, unit costs, cost-to-serve and capacity. Link volumes, service levels, staffing and demand to expense plans; challenge assumptions and identify productivity and operating-leverage opportunities while protecting controls and customer outcomes.
Partner with COO leaders to connect strategic priorities, transformation and operating performance to financial outcomes. Assess cross-business initiatives and execution risks, balancing near-term commitments with longer-term value.
Provide oversight and independent challenge of reporting, controls, allocations and accounting. Reinforce direct and shared cost ownership, reliable management information and consistent financial treatment; resolve issues with Finance and enterprise partners.

Founded in Vancouver in 2016, FORM is the sports technology company behind the award-winning FORM Smart Swim Goggles. Since launching in 2019, our goggles have earned global recognition, including Red Dot, iF Design, and Global Triathlon awards, and are trusted by professional athletes, age-group triathletes, and swimmers looking to get better.

We're a talented, tight-knit team that's fun to work with and serious about building great products. Together, we bring decades of consumer product experience spanning sports eyewear, interface design, and activity-tracking algorithms.

To learn more, visit formswim.com

The Opportunity

Reporting to the CEO, you'll own FORM's finance function end to end. You'll start by learning how our accounting function runs today, then partner with the team to strengthen controls and streamline processes as we grow. From there, you'll lean into financial modelling and become a strategic partner to the executive team.

You'll work directly alongside the CEO, with access to our fractional CFO for mentorship. You'll have real ownership over how FORM plans, reports, and grows, and the support to step up as the role expands. This role requires a hands-on leader who likes being close to the numbers.

What You'll Own

Lead a two-person accounting team, managing our Senior Accountant and supporting the development of the Accountant on their team
Work with the team to put scalable internal controls in place for accurate, reliable financial statements
Own cash and cashflow planning across short- and long-term horizons
Partner with the executive team to build annual budgets, forecasts, and department-specific KPI reporting
Build financial models and scenario plans to support strategic decisions and fundraising
Support the CEO on investor materials and Board and shareholder reporting
Manage tax, audit, legal, and banking partners, and keep FORM compliant across jurisdictions

What Great Looks Like

Reliable reporting generated in hours, not days
A controls environment the executive team trusts
Budgets and KPI reports that department leads use to run their teams
AI embedded in our finance workflows, so the team spends less time on manual tasks and more on insights

The Landscape

Inventory across multi-warehouse global operations
Multiple entities (Canada and US) and multiple currencies
Startup financing, including SAFEs, convertible notes, and equity and debt rounds

How We Work

Daring - Greatness lies just outside our comfort zone. You bring fresh ideas and aren't afraid to try something new
Focused - We're not afraid of throwing out great ideas to execute the right one. You know which numbers matter most and keep the team pointed at them
Human - Work as a team, work for one another, listen to our members. You make finance approachable and explain the numbers so every FORMie can act on them
Learn Fast, Act Fast - Improve through trial, testing and action. You move with urgency, learn from each cycle, and keep improving how finance works

Required Skills & Qualifications

CPA or equivalent, with 7-10 years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leading and developing a team in a Director-level role at a growing startup
Experience with hardware and SaaS business models, including a strong understanding of SaaS KPIs
Strong financial modelling skills and the ability to turn data into decisions
A proven record of accurate internal and external financial and KPI reporting in a complex, multi-currency environment
Experience with employee stock option plans (ESOPs), including administration and cap table management
Experience supporting equity and debt financing processes
Canadian, US, and international tax and accounting experience, including Canadian grants and tax credits such as SR&ED
Strong storytelling skills that turn financial data into insights people can act on

Consumer electronics, fitness, or wearables experience
